subject.title: Feature: Postcondition checks for cron jobs (deterministic verification of agent outcomes)

question: Should OpenClaw add scheduler-owned cron postconditions that execute deterministic commands after agentTurn jobs, or should maintainers first expose a fail-capable plugin hook for post-run verification?
rationale: The issue asks for new command execution, retry, escalation, and persisted state semantics inside cron; source inspection shows the gap is real, but the security boundary and core-vs-plugin ownership cannot be chosen safely by cleanup automation.

options.title: Approve scheduler-owned postconditions
options.body: Add an opt-in CronJob verifier contract with explicit permissions, bounded command execution, state/log/protocol projections, retry context injection, and failure-alert behavior.

options.title: Expose a fail-capable plugin hook first
options.body: Keep core lean by adding a post-run hook that can request scheduler-owned retry or escalation, then implement verifier packages outside core.

options.title: Defer native verification
options.body: Keep command cron and external monitors as the supported path for now, accepting that successful-but-incomplete agent cron runs remain hard to detect automatically.

recommendation.title: Approve scheduler-owned postconditions
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in CronJob verifier contract with explicit permissions, bounded command execution, state/log/protocol projections, retry context injection, and failure-alert behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The central decision crosses cron runtime, docs, state, failure alerts, and user-facing scheduler semantics where steipete has the strongest recent history signal.
